sam: Heads-up — the Go SDK sample app's generator + streaming cancel semantics are tripping people up in onboarding.
priya: details? we thought ctx cancellation went all the way through.
sam: it does not atm. sample app does: `gen := client.NewGenerator(...); stream, _ := gen.Stream(ctx, req)` then user cancels ctx but the underlying HTTP stream keeps running until the generator drains.
marco: that's probably because our Stream() spawns a goroutine that doesn't select on ctx when writing to the out channel. seen that pattern before.
sam: yeah. also auth refresh races with cancel. token refresh can trigger a retry that replays the request even after ctx.Done().
priya: oof. that means callers see extra outputs or duplicate partial chunks. bad for billing + UX.
sam: minimal repro in sample-app:```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 300*time.Millisecond)
defer cancel()
gen := client.NewGenerator(opt)
stream, err := gen.Stream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { return err }
for chunk := range stream.Ch() { fmt.Println(chunk.Text) }
// cancel happens but stream goroutine still tries to send to stream.Ch() after ctx cancelled
```
marco: two angles: 1) Make Stream(ctx, ...) close the returned channel when ctx done. 2) Ensure internal HTTP retry loop checks ctx before retrying.
priya: API ergonomics question: should gen.Stream accept ctx on creation or return a cancellable handle? currently it returns a "Stream" struct with Ch() and Err(), no Cancel(). callers expect context-first pattern.
sam: proposal: Stream(ctx, req) -> returns (Stream, error) and Stream.Close() (or Cancel()) that cancels underlying request. Also have Stream.Ch() be non-blocking with backpressure hints.
marco: alternative is to make generator return io.ReadCloser-like iterator: ReadChunk() that respects ctx on each call. the sample app can still range over it with `for { c, err := stream.ReadChunk(ctx); ... }`. that keeps cancel explicit.
priya: whichever we pick, update sample-app and quickstart to show best practice (use ctx, call Close on signal handlers). new users are copying that code directly.
dev-ci-bot: deploy: go-sdk v0.11.3 published to internal staging at 1753467950 :rocket:
sam: also file a small DX bug: missing example for token-refresh+ctx interplay in auth.md. people need to know we check ctx before retrying.
marco: I'll draft a tiny change: add ctx-check in retry loop + add Stream.Close() wrapper. then PR to go-sdk and update sample-app.
priya: thanks — can you also add a unit test simulating cancel during token refresh (mock transport that blocks then unblocks)? catches regressions.
sam: perfect. I'll update the quickstart snippet and note the cancellation story in the release notes.
marco: assigning to @marco on the SDK PR, tagging @devops for a staging run.
priya: sounds good. small follow-up: should the generator ergonomics prefer channels or iterator? leaning iterator for explicit error handling and ctx per call.
sam: agree. channels are nicer for simple cases but hide backpressure and error ordering. iterator wins for robustness.
priya: cool — I'll revise the sample repo accordingly.
